## BrowserPeerConnections

```k,ignore
@ClientOnly
public service BrowserPeerConnections implements PeerConnections
```

The standard [`PeerConnections`](#peerconnections), over the browser's
`RTCPeerConnection` with perfect negotiation.

**Members**

- `var isSupported: Bool`
  See [`PeerConnections.isSupported`](#peerconnections).
- `func connect(signalling: Channel<Signal, Signal, RpcOnlyError>, iceServers: List<IceServer>, policy: IcePolicy = .all, lifetime: CaptureLifetime = .owner) async throws PeerError -> PeerConnection`
  See [`PeerConnections.connect(signalling:iceServers:policy:lifetime:)`](#peerconnections).

## DataChannel

```k,ignore
@ClientOnly
public class DataChannel<T>
```

One typed data channel of a [`PeerConnection`](#peerconnection)
(`docs/design/46-media-and-rtc.md`, "Typed data channels"). Messages
are encoded like rpc messages, and each side checks that the other's
type has the same shape when it opens.

**Members**

- `let messages: Stream<T>`
  Every message the peer sends, in order for `.reliable`; ends when
  the channel or its connection closes. Read once.
- `var isOpen: Bool`
  Whether messages can be sent now; reactive.
- `func send(_ message: T) async throws DataChannelError`
  Sends `message`, waiting first while more than 1 MiB is buffered or
  until the channel opens.

  - Throws: [`DataChannelError.tooLarge`](#datachannelerror) over 64 KiB encoded,
    `.incompatible` when the peer's message type differs, `.closed`.
- `func close()`
  Closes this channel.

## DataChannelError

```k,ignore
public enum DataChannelError implements Error, Equatable
```

Why a [`DataChannel`](#datachannel) message couldn't be sent.

**Members**

- `case closed`
  The channel or its connection closed.
- `case tooLarge(limit: Int)`
  The encoded message is over `limit` bytes (64 KiB).
- `case incompatible`
  The peer runs a build whose message type has another shape.

## DataChannelKind

```k,ignore
public struct DataChannelKind<T> where T implements Codable
```

A data channel paired with the type of its messages
(`docs/design/46-media-and-rtc.md`, "Typed data channels"):
`let chatLines: DataChannelKind<ChatLine> = DataChannelKind(name: "chat")`.

Both peers open the channel of a kind independently, in any order: its
id is derived from the name. Kinds with the same name are the same
channel and must carry the same type (K2408), and two names whose ids
collide are K2409.

**Members**

- `init(name: String)`
  Creates the kind named `name`.

  - Parameter name: a string literal.
- `var name: String`
  The channel's name.

## Delivery

```k,ignore
public enum Delivery implements Equatable
```

How a data channel delivers its messages.

**Members**

- `case reliable`
  Ordered and retransmitted until delivered.
- `case unordered(retransmits: Int)`
  In any order, retransmitted at most `retransmits` times: positions
  and other values where only the latest matters.

## IcePolicy

```k,ignore
public enum IcePolicy implements Equatable
```

Which network paths a [`PeerConnection`](#peerconnection) may use.

**Members**

- `case all`
  Direct paths, and a TURN relay when there is no other.
- `case relayOnly`
  Only through a TURN relay: for testing a deployment's TURN server,
  and for users who must not reveal their address to the peer.

## IceServer

```k,ignore
public struct IceServer implements Codable, Equatable
```

A STUN or TURN server a browser may use to reach its peer
(`docs/design/46-media-and-rtc.md`, "STUN and TURN without third-party
accounts"), as [`IceServers.forClient(user:validFor:)`](#iceservers) issues them.

**Members**

- `let urls: List<String>`
  `stun:`, `turn:` and `turns:` URLs (RFC 7064 and 7065). They have
  no `//` and no `http` scheme, so they are text, not `Url`s;
  [`TurnConfig`](#turnconfig) checks their schemes at startup.
- `let username: String? = nil`
  The TURN user name, `<expiry>:<user>`.
- `let credential: String? = nil`
  The short-lived TURN credential. It is meant for the browser and
  expires, so it isn't a `Secret`.

## IceServers

```k,ignore
@ServerOnly
public service IceServers
```

Issues the ICE servers a browser connects through, with short-lived
TURN credentials (`docs/design/46-media-and-rtc.md`, "STUN and TURN
without third-party accounts"). Server-only: the secret they are signed
with stays in [`TurnConfig`](#turnconfig).

There is no default STUN or TURN server: with no `K_TURN_URLS` it
issues none, and browsers on one machine or one network reach each
other directly.

**Members**

- `func forClient(user: String, validFor: Duration) async -> List<IceServer>`
  The servers for `user`, valid for `validFor`: one entry with every
  `K_TURN_URLS` URL and a credential in coturn's TURN REST scheme (the
  user name `<expiry>:<user>`, the credential the Base64 HMAC-SHA1 of
  the user name under `K_TURN_SECRET`), or none when no URL is set.

## MediaSender

```k,ignore
@ClientOnly
public class MediaSender
```

The tracks a [`PeerConnection`](#peerconnection) sends from one stream.

**Members**

- `func replace(with stream: MediaStream)`
  Sends `stream`'s tracks instead, with no renegotiation where the
  browser allows it: switching cameras, starting a screen share.
- `func stop()`
  Stops sending these tracks; the peer's copies end with
  `.remoteEnded`.

## PeerClose

```k,ignore
public enum PeerClose implements Equatable
```

Why a [`PeerConnection`](#peerconnection) closed.

**Members**

- `case byApp`
  The app called `close()`, or its owner went away.
- `case byPeer`
  The peer hung up.
- `case failed`
  The network didn't recover within 15 seconds.
- `case signallingLost`
  The signalling channel closed for good.

## PeerConnection

```k,ignore
@ClientOnly
public class PeerConnection
```

A call with one peer (`docs/design/46-media-and-rtc.md`,
"`PeerConnections` and `PeerConnection`"). Its fields are reactive.

Negotiation is the stdlib's ("perfect negotiation"): adding a stream,
opening a data channel and restarting ICE after a network change need
no app code. A handle, not a value; it closes with its owner.

**Members**

- `var state: PeerState`
  `.waitingForPeer`, `.connecting`, `.connected`, `.reconnecting` or
  `.closed` and why.
- `var remote: MediaStream?`
  What the peer sends; `nil` until its first track arrives.
- `func send(_ stream: MediaStream) -> MediaSender`
  Sends every track of `stream` to the peer.

  - Returns: the sender, to replace the tracks or stop sending them.
- `func channel<T>(_ kind: DataChannelKind<T>, delivery: Delivery = .reliable) -> DataChannel<T>`
  A typed data channel named by `kind`. Both peers open it, in any
  order.

  - Parameter delivery: `.reliable` (ordered, retransmitted), or
    `.unordered(retransmits:)` where only the latest matters.
- `func stats() async -> PeerStats`
  Round-trip time, bitrate, packet loss, and whether a relay is in
  use.
- `func close()`
  Hangs up: the peer sees `.closed(.byPeer)`. Closing a closed
  connection does nothing.

## PeerConnections

```k,ignore
@Platform(side: .client)
public interface PeerConnections
```

Peer-to-peer calls (`docs/design/46-media-and-rtc.md`, "Peer
connections"). A client-only platform interface:
[`BrowserPeerConnections`](#browserpeerconnections) is injected with no `use` rule, and
[`k.test.TestPeerConnections`](k-test.md#testpeerconnections) replaces it in tests.

**Members**

- `var isSupported: Bool`
  Whether this browser can make calls: `false` without
  `RTCPeerConnection`, and during server rendering.
- `func connect(signalling: Channel<Signal, Signal, RpcOnlyError>, iceServers: List<IceServer>, policy: IcePolicy = .all, lifetime: CaptureLifetime = .owner) async throws PeerError -> PeerConnection`
  Connects to the peer at the other end of `signalling`, the channel
  the app's protocol opened to a [`SignallingRelay`](#signallingrelay).

  Waits until the relay pairs this peer with another, then returns
  the connection in `.connecting`; media and data flow once it is
  `.connected`. The stdlib runs the whole negotiation.

  - Parameters:
    - iceServers: the servers [`IceServers`](#iceservers) issued; empty on one
      machine or one network.
    - policy: `.relayOnly` sends everything through TURN.
    - lifetime: `.owner` closes the connection, and the channel, when
      the run that connected is cancelled.
  - Throws: [`PeerError.unsupported`](#peererror), or `.signallingClosed` when the
    channel ended before a peer joined.

## PeerError

```k,ignore
public enum PeerError implements Error, Equatable
```

Why [`PeerConnections.connect(signalling:iceServers:policy:lifetime:)`](#peerconnections)
failed.

**Members**

- `case unsupported`
  No `RTCPeerConnection` in this browser.
- `case signallingClosed`
  The channel ended before a peer joined.

## PeerState

```k,ignore
public enum PeerState implements Equatable
```

Where a [`PeerConnection`](#peerconnection) is.

**Members**

- `case waitingForPeer`
  The peer left the room; a new one may join.
- `case connecting`
  Negotiating, before media and data flow.
- `case connected`
  Media and data flow.
- `case reconnecting`
  The network changed; ICE restarts through the same channel, and
  after 15 seconds without recovery the connection closes `.failed`.
- `case closed(PeerClose)`
  Over, for good.

## PeerStats

```k,ignore
public struct PeerStats implements Equatable
```

A snapshot of a [`PeerConnection`](#peerconnection)'s network, from `stats()`.

**Members**

- `let roundTripTime: Duration?`
  The round-trip time of the path in use; `nil` before one is chosen.
- `let outgoingBitrate: Int?`
  The bits per second the path can send, as the browser estimates
  it; `nil` when unknown.
- `let packetsLost: Int`
  The packets lost of what was received, every track together.
- `let isRelayed: Bool`
  Whether the path in use goes through a TURN relay.

## RelayPeer

```k,ignore
@ServerOnly
public class RelayPeer
```

One peer of a [`SignallingRelay`](#signallingrelay) room, a lease of the request that
joined (`docs/design/46-media-and-rtc.md`, "Signalling over a channel").

**Members**

- `let signals: Stream<Signal>`
  What this peer receives: the other peer's signals, and the relay's
  own `peerJoined` and `peerLeft`. The handler's `sending` stream.
- `func forward(_ signal: Signal)`
  Forwards one of this peer's signals to the other peers of its room.
- `func leave()`
  Leaves the room now instead of when the request ends; idempotent.

## Signal

```k,ignore
public enum Signal implements Codable, Equatable
```

One message of the signalling between two peers
(`docs/design/46-media-and-rtc.md`, "Signalling over a channel"): the
`C` and `S` of the app's `Channel<Signal, Signal, RpcOnlyError>`.

Opaque to apps. Only [`PeerConnection`](#peerconnection) and [`SignallingRelay`](#signallingrelay) create or
read one; an app passes them through its handler
(`Channel(sending: peer.signals) { signal => peer.forward(signal) }`)
and never builds a session description or parses one.

**Members**

- `case peerJoined`
  The relay: another peer joined this one's room.
- `case peerLeft`
  The relay: the other peer left the room, or its channel closed.
- `case hello(peer: String)`
  A peer's id, sent once per pairing; the two ids decide which peer is
  polite, so a peer that rejoins keeps its role.
- `case description(type: String, sdp: String)`
  A session description, an offer or an answer.
- `case candidate(candidate: String, mid: String?, line: Int?)`
  A network candidate.
- `case bye`
  The peer hung up.

## SignallingRelay

```k,ignore
@ServerOnly
public class SignallingRelay<Key> where Key implements Hashable, Key implements Codable
```

Pairs the peers that join under one key and forwards each one's
[`Signal`](#signal)s to the other (`docs/design/46-media-and-rtc.md`,
"Signalling over a channel"). Held by a `@Scope(.server)` service:

```k,ignore
let relay: SignallingRelay<RoomId> = SignallingRelay(peersPerRoom: 2)
```

It is built on [`k.rpc.Broadcast`](k-rpc.md#broadcast) and [`k.rpc.Presence`](k-rpc.md#presence), so the
peers of a room may be on different replicas, and a peer is a lease of
the request that joined: it leaves when its channel closes.

**Members**

- `init(peersPerRoom: Int = 2)`
  Creates a relay admitting `peersPerRoom` peers under each key.
- `func join(key: Key) async -> RelayPeer?`
  Joins the room `key` for as long as the calling request lives; for a
  channel's handler, until the channel closes.

  - Returns: the peer, whose `signals` the handler sends and whose
    `forward(_:)` its receiving function calls, or `nil` when the room
    already has `peersPerRoom` peers.

## TurnConfig

```k,ignore
public config TurnConfig
```

The deployment's own TURN server (`docs/design/46-media-and-rtc.md`,
"STUN and TURN without third-party accounts"), read by [`IceServers`](#iceservers).
Server-only, like every config.

URLs without a secret are a configuration error at startup, and so is a
URL whose scheme isn't `stun`, `turn` or `turns`.
